title: The viceroy of Sicily to Ferdinand, Messina, 27 Apr 1503: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 94, ff. 120r-121v; homophonic alphabet recovered ciphertext-only and code partly read by Michael Brackx (catalogue item 9)

documents.route: the viceroy of Sicily, Messina -> Ferdinand

transcription.source: Michael Brackx, GitHub issue #62 (21 Oct 2026): ff. 120r, 120v, 121r sign by sign from the repository's Gallica scans, code groups as units; C: lines kept in ct94_brackx.txt
transcription.notes: Transcribed by the contributor with Claude, not by the project. The measured 3,554 tokens include the words of the clear islands. Without them: 2,751 letter signs (all in the 39 key classes), 2 doubtful tokens, 612 code-group tokens (113 distinct), 9 initials or paragraph marks. Brackx counts 2,660 signs. Spot-checked here against the scans of f. 120r ll. 1-3 and f. 121r ll. 1-2: sign for sign as transcribed. Done by eye with Claude; not checked line by line by a second person.

system.summary: A homophonic alphabet of invented signs (39 sign classes for 21 letters) interleaved with nomenclator groups of two to four Latin letters (113 distinct, initials mostly m-, q-, n-, r-, p-), mixed with clear Spanish.
system.sibling_key: Close to the Gran cifra of the Gran Capitan, 1501-04 (Bergenroth's reconstruction: muy = de, against mny = de here; minims n/u are one shape); not the key of no. 93
system.notes: Split on 21 Oct 2026 from esp318no93 (nos. 93-94) under the one-key rule, after Brackx's solution: no. 93's commonest groups (gto x21, pie x19, heg x13, zoe, zoc, hug) never occur in no. 94, and no. 94's (qa x65, rah x61, mny x47, qag x32) are absent from no. 93's stream except pif x2. Code order: not alphabetical (gik = su and nyl = havia sort before mny = de), so a two-part code; 113 distinct groups.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment in the volume or in print (Parisi, Galende Diaz, Tomokiyo, Quirantes); Brackx found none either.

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Michael Brackx directed Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) and sent the result as GitHub issue #62. The project (Daniel Bourdeau with Claude) checked it against the scans and with its own controls, and split the entry.
tools: Brackx's scripts (numpy simulated annealing against a Spanish character 5-gram from the Quijote; not in the repository)
check94.py (review: decode with his key, shuffled-key and shuffled-text annealing controls, word coverage, code inventories)

solution.what: No. 94 (ff. 120r-121v) located in the volume with nos. 93 and 95; no decipherment anywhere in it. Sampled code groups only; the letter was left untranscribed (then part of esp318, later esp318no93).
Michael Brackx (issue #62) transcribed ff. 120r-121r sign by sign with code groups as units (2,660 signs, 612 groups by his count).

Brackx: code groups set aside, the single signs annealed as homophonic substitution against a Spanish 5-gram, eight starts; 3-5 starts converge on one key at -2.61 nats/char. Suspect classes cropped from the scans (254 + 149 occurrences) and split (ß = u/v, thorn = i, capital B = p, tall S = g, small 5 = n, crossed f = c, ff-stroke = s); the split classes re-solved from scratch recover the same values.

Brackx: code groups read from context over three rounds: about 20 firm (qa que, rah y, mny de, mys en, mnb la, pif no, qag se, nae los, nyb lo, pat por, lux como, qe quando, nyl havia, gik su, reg yo, mnh gente, qaz V. Al., pns Puerto-, malg/malh ll) and about 14 tentative; mys first read la, corrected to en from 'estava en Seminara'.
Brackx: one-part (alphabetical) nomenclator tested on the firm readings and rejected (gik = su and nyl = havia sort before mny = de).
Review here: Brackx's transcription compared sign by sign with the scans of f. 120r ll. 1-3 and f. 121r ll. 1-2 (groups rag, re, lux, mog, nyl, pat, mas, qar, qag, lik, pns as he has them).

Review here (check94.py, es-golden-age order 5): his key gives -2.59 nats/char on the letter-sign runs; the letter's own clear islands -2.23; 200 shuffled-value keys best -4.48. An independent anneal (with a letter-frequency penalty) from four random starts reaches his key in two (35 of the 40 sign labels agree, -2.58); the same annealer on the shuffled-order text reaches only -3.63 to -3.77. Word coverage (Spanish words of 4+ letters): 0.63 against 0.77 for the clear islands and 0.10-0.13 for shuffled keys.

Review here: code inventories of nos. 93 and 94 compared (ct93_eye.txt trigrams against ct94_brackx.txt groups). No. 93's top groups gto, pie, heg, zoe, zoc, hug never occur in no. 94; no. 94's qa, rah, mny, qag do not occur in no. 93 (pif twice). muy occurs three times in no. 93 against mny 47 times in no. 94. Different keys; no. 94 split into its own entry. The g- initials of the earlier sample were q- (the same 9-shaped letter).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3127 tokens, 58 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.351 per letter; random keys -4.578 (z 8.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.12 (mean -3.154, z 27.5); annealer on the real text -2.374. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Brackx's sign transcription ct94_brackx.txt; his normalised decryption is only in issue #62 (linked; a copy in the folder is still needed)

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the repository holds only the sign transcription; Brackx's provisional decryption (issue #62) has holes in most sentences around about 90 open code groups. Per-document grade D confirmed; no. 94 relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read; method -> not solved; fraction_read 0.929 -> 0. The ciphertext-only alphabet recovery is unaffected.
Brackx's interlinear decipherment and his v3 normalized reading copied from GitHub issue #62 into texts/no94_decryption.md and texts/no94_partial_reading.md (hole notation converted, nothing added).

Bergenroth's Gran cifra list (BNE MSS 20.211/52), thought not online, read from Arturo Quirantes's 2018 photocopy and transcription of the sheet (about 75 code groups, texts/bergenroth_gran_cifra_codes.tsv) and compared with no. 94 (research/reading_audit/b27_esp94_berg.py): 1 of 12 comparable firm readings agrees (mny/muy = de), 11 differ (que qa/raz, se qag/pix, no pif/quem, lo nyb/pux, como lux/mad, por pat/rau ...). Not this letter's code. Six open no. 94 groups share a Bergenroth spelling (nnl era, li aun, nym en, luy capitan, nen para, nol es): not adopted, flagged for review.
Partial reading scored (b17_score.py, es): 0.157 clean (13/83), explicit holes 0.253 (21/83). The holes are mostly code groups without a key. Kept decoded, not read.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.351; polyphony 0.0; 269 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.374

outcome.method_basis: Michael Brackx recovered the 39-class homophonic alphabet ciphertext-only (annealing the letter signs against a Spanish 5-gram, no crib), and it reproduces here from random starts; but about 90 code groups are open and his provisional decryption (issue #62, not copied into the folder) has holes in most sentences, so no reading is claimed (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026). With the code read the method would be key recovered from ciphertext-only.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: no. 94, the only document, is decoded, not read, so no tokens are in a document that reads. The earlier 0.929 (ct94_brackx.txt: 3,127 of 3,365 cipher tokens given a value or a firm code reading) is withdrawn as a reading figure. 23 Oct 2026 (b27): still 0: the partial reading (texts/no94_partial_reading.md) scores 0.157 clean.

gaps.item: about 90 code groups, 154 of 623 code-group tokens, mostly once or twice
gaps.detail: two-part code, so neighbours do not bracket meanings; Bergenroth's Gran cifra list (BNE MSS 20.211/52, read 23 Oct 2026 from Quirantes's photocopy) is a different code (1 of 12 comparable firm readings agrees); the 'Cifra del visorrey' (BRAH 9/15 ff. 1-6) is not digitised

gaps.item: 14 tentative code readings (93 tokens): mog, lik, pnb, pad, re, mok, mas, pit, leg, nag, neb, per, nob, mos
gaps.detail: one or two good contexts each; kept as Brackx's tentative values; no key to confirm them

gaps.item: spelled-out stretches that do not parse (about a fifth of the letter-sign text)
gaps.detail: single misread glyphs in a transcription by eye; about a third of the ß/thorn/B glyphs not cropped and checked; sign K unstable (l or s). Not re-checked on the scans in b27: the code holes alone keep every second sentence open, so a cleaner letter stream would not make the letter read

outcome.notes: Status: in progress. The content (Seminara and its aftermath, Portocarrero's death, Hugo de Cardona's faction, 800 peones, a proposed election among the captains) is readable in outline; single words stay provisional. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no. 94 decoded, not read (about 90 code groups open, holes in most sentences); class read in part -> not read, method -> not solved; the ciphertext-only alphabet stands.

texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b27): no decipherment in the volume, in print or on DECODE. Brackx's decipherment copied into texts/no94_decryption.md and his v3 reading into texts/no94_partial_reading.md (hole notation converted, nothing added): 0.157 clean (13/83), explicit holes 0.253. Bergenroth's Gran cifra list (BNE MSS 20.211/52) read from Arturo Quirantes's 2018 photocopy (texts/bergenroth_gran_cifra_codes.tsv) and tested: 1 of 12 comparable firm readings agrees (mny/muy = de), 11 differ (qa/raz que, qag/pix se, pif/quem no, nyb/pux lo ...), so it is not this letter's code. Blocker: no-key-material (154 unread code-group tokens, one or two per sentence; the 'Cifra del visorrey', BRAH 9/15 ff. 1-6, is not digitised).
texts.label: no. 94, ff. 120r-121r, the viceroy of Sicily to Ferdinand, Messina, 27 Apr 1503
texts.summary: The viceroy of Sicily reports from Messina, the day before Cerignola and six days after Andrada's victory at Seminara: the galley could not cross the Faro, a night entry with the infantry looting, a pesquisa under oath into the spoil, three principal prisoners kept in the castle until the king orders, and the dispute over the post Portocarrero had given after his death. Michael Brackx's decipherment and normalised reading (provisional word by word, GitHub issue #62) are copied into texts/.
